title: Runtime release train notes — Safe apply + rollback (Optimization Config) — enablement & backports
body:
Purpose
- Coordinate the runtime release train and cross-repo sequencing needed to enable the Safe apply + rollback feature flag for Optimization Config changes (batching/caching/quant profiles).
- Capture what must land before enablement, our backport policy, and a quick risk assessment for the Feb limited GA window.

Context / target
- Feature: versioned “Optimization Config” + safe apply workflow w/ gates + one-click rollback.
- Target: internal beta now → limited GA (selected Hosted/Dedicated accounts) in 2026-02 to 2026-03.
- Critical property: runtime config application must be idempotent + race-safe, otherwise rollback cannot be trusted.

Release train assumptions (runtime)
- Runtime train: weekly cut (Tue), hotfix window (as needed) with approval from Release Eng + Runtime on-call.
- We will NOT enable the feature by default at runtime ship time; enablement is controlled via server-side flags + allowlist in control plane (blast radius managed by Control Plane / SRE).

Feature flags (names as used in config)
- runtime.optimization_config.safe_apply_enabled (default: false)
- runtime.optimization_config.rollback_enabled (default: false)
- control_plane.optimization_config.versioning_enabled (default: false)
- console.optimization_config.history_ui_enabled (default: false)
- console.optimization_config.rollback_button_enabled (default: false)

Definition of “ready to enable” (minimum bar)
1) Runtime correctness (hard gate)
- Idempotent applier in place and deployed broadly (Hosted + Dedicated) with safe retry behavior.
- Apply treated as a transaction/checkpointed: workers should not remain in mixed states after rollback/abort.
- Race between apply and rollback must be handled (winner determined by monotonic “desired version” / epoch).
- Worker cache invalidation does not cause sustained p95 regression beyond allowed thresholds.

2) Control plane / rollout controller (hard gate)
- Control plane can:
  - Create immutable version
  - Validate (schema + semantic)
  - Start canary rollout
  - Evaluate gates (SLO metrics + optional eval quality gate)
  - Pause / resume / abort
  - Trigger rollback to prior version
- Rollout state machine must be resilient to retries and partial failures (controller restarts).

3) Audit + RBAC (hard gate for enterprise accounts)
- Audit events emitted for create/validate/apply/promote/rollback actions.
- RBAC role “optimization change operator” (or equivalent) can perform apply/rollback; read-only roles can view history/diff.
- SIEM export compatibility verified for event payload shape.

4) Observability + operational readiness (hard gate)
- Rollout Health Dashboard panels present + annotated with apply/rollback events.
- Gate metrics tagged with tenant/model/region/config_version.
- Runbooks in place; on-call knows how to rollback and verify recovery.

5) Console UX (soft gate for internal enablement; hard gate for customer enablement)
- For limited GA customers: rollback must be available via Console (button + confirmation + blast radius summary).
- For internal only: API-only rollback is acceptable (but we should not sell/announce without Console).

What needs to land (by repo)
Runtime (redwood)
- PR-19915 runtime-config-apply-transaction
- PR-19918 idempotent-config-applier
- PR-20111 fix rollback race condition (required for enablement)
- PR-19933 add SLO gate hooks (metrics tags) (required)
- NOTE: runtime changes must be deployed BEFORE control-plane starts canary rollouts; otherwise we’ll generate rollout states runtime can’t honor.

Control plane (redwood)
- Version storage + CRUD for immutable versions (baseline)
- Canary rollout controller and pause/resume/abort
- Rollback API endpoint semantics (what “rolled back” means) + idempotency
- Gate evaluation hooks

Console (redwood + console backend)
- History list + diff view + rollback action
- Rollback confirmation modal checks server-side (cooldown, blast radius)

Security / policy
- rbac-policy-bundle PR-20070 add optimization change permissions
- Audit schema: PR-19941 add audit log events for config changes

Observability / gating infra
- observability-pack PR-20012 dashboard panels
- perf-canary PR-20005 perf regression canary job
- slo-toolkit PR-20023 rule library (if used for gates; ensure versions pinned)

Private deployments (not required for Hosted/Dedicated enablement, but impacts messaging)
- redwood-private-installer PR-19972
- redwood-helm-charts PR-19980
- redwood-terraform PR-20103

Sequencing plan (proposed)
Phase 0 — Ship runtime foundations (now → next train)
- Goal: runtime has all correctness fixes behind flags; safe no-op when flag is false.
- Must include: PR-19915, PR-19918, PR-20111, PR-19933.
- Validation: synthetic apply/rollback under load in staging; confirm no worker mixed-state.

Phase 1 — Control plane + audit + RBAC (same week as Phase 0 or immediately after)
- Control plane endpoints and controller can ship “dark” with allowlist.
- Audit/RBAC must ship before any enterprise customer enablement.
- Validation: API-only flows used by Eng/SRE to simulate canary/rollback.

Phase 2 — Observability & canary jobs
- Dashboard annotations + gate alerts wired.
- perf-canary can run in parallel; ensure false-positive thresholds are tuned before customer exposure.

Phase 3 — Console enablement
- Rollback button and history UI behind separate flag.
- Customer-facing enablement requires Console + docs.

Enablement checklist (Go/No-Go for flipping allowlist)
- Runtime version deployed in all relevant regions for the target accounts.
- Control plane controller version deployed and stable for 48h (no crash loops; no stuck rollouts in internal test).
- Audit events verified end-to-end:
  - event emitted
  - appears in audit log UI / export
  - contains: actor, action, config_version_from/to, scope, request_id, timestamp
- RBAC policy deployed; test account with “operator” can rollback; read-only cannot.
- Dashboard “Optimization rollout health” shows tagged metrics; annotations visible.
- Runbook reviewed by on-call; incident-bot shortcut points to correct place.
- Support enablement: how to identify active config version per tenant/model/region.

Backport strategy
Policy
- We will backport ONLY bug fixes that affect safety/correctness of apply/rollback, audit completeness, or gate metric integrity.
- We will NOT backport new UX improvements, non-critical refactors, or optional features (e.g., additional diff highlighting).

Backport candidates (expected)
- Rollback race condition fixes (PR-20111 class) — YES
- Idempotency edge cases under retries — YES
- Missing metrics tags for gate evaluation — YES
- Audit event omissions for rollback/apply — YES
- Minor console copy changes — NO (unless correctness/legal)

Backport process
- Runtime: runtime sponsor (Mateo/Noah) approves; Release Eng (Connor) schedules hotfix train if needed.
- Control plane: Ethan’s team approves; avoid mixing multiple unrelated fixes in one hotfix.
- Console: Chloe’s team; hotfix only if blocks rollback execution or misrepresents blast radius.

Test expectations for backports
- Minimum: targeted integration tests + e2e in staging with failure injection (controller restart, worker restart, concurrent apply+rollback).
- Sahana to sign off on CI signal quality (flake risk).

Risk assessment (current)
R1: Mixed worker states after rollback (SEV risk)
- Impact: rollback “succeeds” but partial fleet stays on bad config → sustained latency/5xx.
- Mitigation: require PR-20111 and regression tests; staging gameday; gate rollout progression on worker convergence.

R2: Gate false positives cause stuck rollouts (operational pain)
- Impact: canary pauses too often; on-call fatigue; customers lose confidence.
- Mitigation: conservative default thresholds; “manual override with justification” path; tune in internal beta before limited GA.

R3: Cache invalidation during rollback causes transient p95 spike
- Impact: rollback mitigates regression but induces its own latency blip.
- Mitigation: rollout controller limits shard size; runtime gradual cache warm; document expected transient behavior.

R4: Audit gaps (enterprise blocker)
- Impact: customer flags missing rollback event (seen before), procurement/security escalation.
- Mitigation: audit event contract tests; verify export pipeline; add alert on missing event types for enabled tenants.

R5: Cross-version compatibility (runtime vs control plane)
- Impact: control plane issues config versions that older runtime misinterprets.
- Mitigation: versioned schema w/ strict validation; runtime advertises supported schema version; control plane blocks apply if incompatible.

Open questions / decisions needed this week
- Do we require Console rollback UI for internal beta accounts, or allow API-only? (Proposal: API-only OK for internal; Console required for limited GA.)
- Cooldown policy: how soon can a rollback be triggered after an apply? (Proposal: allow immediate rollback; only restrict repeated toggling within N minutes unless SRE override.)
- Blast radius definition for “scope” in confirmation modal: tenant+model+region+%? Ensure server-side computed summary, not client-side.

Owners / points of contact
- Release coordination: Connor O’Brien
- Runtime: Noah Patel (primary), Omar El-Sayed (secondary)
- Control plane: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
- Console: Chloe Martin / Jada Williams
- SRE readiness: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello
- Security/RBAC/audit: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei

Next steps (as of 2026-02-01)
- Connor: confirm runtime train includes PR-20111 and PR-19933; schedule staging verification run.
- Noah + Sahana: run apply→pause→rollback under synthetic load; capture p95 and worker convergence screenshots/logs.
- Ethan: confirm controller + rollback endpoint deployed to staging; validate “abort vs rollback” semantics.
- Marcus: confirm RBAC bundle deployed and tested with enterprise role set.
- Sean: confirm dashboard panels + annotations are present; update on-call checklist for enablement.

Notes / log (running)
- If we need a hotfix: prefer a single-purpose runtime hotfix containing only rollback correctness fix + tests.
- For limited GA: keep allowlist small and only on regions where runtime version is verified (avoid mixed runtime versions across regions for same tenant if possible).
